source: Dr. Scott Lynn slides (Carolinas PGA 2019), table credited to McGhie (unpublished data)
population: 23 golfers, 86 driver swings; club speed 109.6 +/- 3.6 mph
metric: share of pressure on lead (front) foot
measurement_type: MEASURED pressure (unpublished data in a presentation; not peer reviewed)
implication_for_gate: most swings are heavily lead-loaded at impact, but the range reaches 3.6%, so a load-based 'lead foot planted' gate would fail some real swings

source: PING study (Shephard & Henrikson) in the same Lynn slides
metric: dominant ground-force style per swing (z-score vs tour averages)
value: vertical 351 swings (36%); torque 105 (11%); horizontal 513 (53%); tour average vertical printed as '179 +/- 20.0 BW'
implication_for_gate: vertical-dominant ('push up') swings are about a third of swings, so a gate must not fail upward lead-leg drive
flags: the '179 BW' unit is printed as BW; probably %BW, unverified

source: Koenig, Tamres & Mann (MIT Newman Lab), ISBS proceedings, 'An analysis of the kinetics and kinematics of the golf swing'
population: 14 golfers in 3 handicap groups (0-7, 8-14, 15+); driver, 3-iron, 7-iron; artificial turf on a force plate; shoes tracked with LED arrays
value: 'the shoes exhibited significant movement, with the high handicappers having the greatest total amount of movement'; vertical force reaches a minimum shortly after impact for both feet
numeric: no (no displacement numbers in the paper)
implication_for_gate: shoe movement is normal even in good players, and less in better players; post-impact unloading of both feet is typical
flags: year not printed in the extracted text

source: Ball, Best, Dowlan & Brown, ISBS 2002, 'Different weight transfer patterns in golf'
value: Front Foot group (n=28): CoP at ball contact 76% toward front foot, 65% heel-to-toe; Reverse group (n=12): 43% toward front foot, 76% toward toes
units: % of stance width / % of foot length
implication_for_gate: a 'Reverse' style (weight back at contact) exists with no handicap or clubhead-speed difference, so the gate should not require lead-foot loading
flags: CoP position, not foot lift or slip

source: Worsfold, Smith & Dyson, J Sports Sci Med (PMC3794489)
population: 24 right-handed males (hcp 0-26), natural-grass force platforms, 3 shoe designs
metric: shear/vertical ratio ('coefficient of friction' = (|Fx|+|Fy|)/Fz) and peak vertical force
value: 0.62 +/- 0.03 at back and front foot, regardless of shoe or club; driver Fz max (metal spikes) back foot 0.33 BW, front foot 0.83 BW
implication_for_gate: sim foot-ground friction must hold a shear/vertical ratio around 0.62 without sliding; slip in the sim at lower ratios is a physics artefact, not a style

source: GOLF.com Swing Study, Jack Nicklaus (Mike Malaska), 2020-01-21
metric: lead heel lifts on the backswing and is 'slammed' down to start the downswing
implication_for_gate: the heel is already up at the top and moves DOWN in the top-to-impact window; measure lift against address, not the top, or this style fails

metric: lead heel lifted off the ground
implication_for_gate: same as Nicklaus: allow heel-only lift
flags: the article does not say exactly when in the swing

metric: lifts the left foot, plants it, lifts the right foot, then starts the swing
implication_for_gate: happens before takeaway, outside the top-to-impact window; the gate must start at the top, not at address
flags: the article describes a pre-swing move, not an impact-time jump

metric: lead foot pressure moves toe to heel and 'most of [his] shoe [is] in the air' near the bottom of the swing; the lead foot then 'comes even higher off the ground' and repositions
implication_for_gate: partial lead-foot lift near impact is legit at elite level, so the gate must allow part of the foot off the ground at impact
flags: in-window exception; the strongest reason not to require full flat contact at impact

population: one tour player, club speed quoted 118.2 mph
metric: trail heel off early; 'pushing hard off the ground with his lead foot'
implication_for_gate: vertical push off the lead foot is a legit power style

source: Golf Digest (David Leadbetter), Gary Woodland analysis
population: one tour player (123.2 mph club speed quoted)
metric: 'his left foot, how it spins and moves back to the left'
implication_for_gate: lead-foot spin and slide after impact is legit; keep post-impact out of the gate

source: Golf Smart Academy (Tyler Ferrell), Patrick Reed swing analysis
metric: lead foot 'appears to replant in a slightly more closed position before impact', then keeps 'rotating and sliding behind him as he releases'
implication_for_gate: a small replant or yaw before impact exists in a major winner, so a zero-slip gate is too strict; size it to catch skating, not replants
flags: the article calls excess lead-foot spin a possible accuracy cost, not a fault per se
